summary.text: In botany, a fruit is the seed-bearing structure of a flowering plant, formed from the ovary after flowering.
Fruits are how flowering plants spread their seeds, and edible ones use humans and other animals to do it.
Botanically, nuts, bean pods, corn kernels, tomatoes and wheat grains all count as fruits, though everyday language does not call them that.

facts.label: Outer layer
facts.value: The pericarp, which usually forms from the ovary

facts.label: Accessory fruits
facts.value: Include apple, rose hip, strawberry and pineapple

facts.label: Cereal grains
facts.value: Corn, rice and wheat are a kind of fruit

items.prompt: A cook files a tomato under vegetables. How would a botanist classify it?

options.label: A fruit, because it is a ripened ovary holding seeds
A vegetable, because it tastes savoury, not sweet
A seed, because it is a ripened ovule
A nut, because it has a hard shell

items.explain: In botany a fruit is a ripened ovary that contains seeds, and a tomato is one, even though cooks call it a vegetable.

items.prompt: Rhubarb often fills pies the way fruit does. What part of the plant are you actually eating?

options.label: The ripened ovary, as with an apple
The leaf stalk, or petiole
The seed, as with a grain of wheat
The root, where the plant stores food

items.explain: Rhubarb is often called a fruit in pies, but its edible produce is the leaf stalk of the plant.

items.prompt: A baker mills wheat. Botanically the grain is a fruit, yet the flour comes almost entirely from the seed. Why?

options.label: The fruit wall falls away before harvest
Wheat makes seeds without any ovary
The fruit wall is thin and fused to the seed coat
The fruit is fleshy and gets thrown away

items.explain: A cereal grain is a kind of fruit, but its wall is thin and fused to the seed coat, so almost all of the edible grain is actually seed.

items.prompt: As a berry ripens, the wall of its ovary can turn fleshy; in a nut it turns hard. What is this ovary wall called?

options.label: The endosperm, which feeds the embryo
The style, which guides the pollen tube
The stigma, which receives the pollen
The pericarp

items.explain: As the ovules develop into seeds, the ovary ripens and the ovary wall, the pericarp, may become fleshy or form a hard covering.

items.prompt: Parts of a flower besides the ovary, such as fused petals and sepals, ripen with it into a big part of the fruit. What is this fruit called?

options.label: An accessory fruit
A multiple fruit
A syncarpous fruit
An apocarpous fruit

items.explain: When floral parts other than the ovary form a significant part of the fruit, it is called an accessory fruit.

items.prompt: A bear eats ripe berries and wanders off. How do both the plant and the bear gain?

options.label: The plant is pollinated, and the bear finds shelter
The plant gets nutrients back, and the bear gets seeds to eat
The plant's seeds are carried away, and the bear gets food
The plant keeps its fruit longer, and the bear loses weight

items.explain: Edible fruits and animals have a symbiotic relationship: seed dispersal for the plant and nutrition for the animal.
